story.title: Hayden Panettiere, actress known for 'Heroes' and 'Nashville,' dies at 36
story.summary: Hayden Panettiere, the actress famous for her roles in 'Heroes' and 'Nashville,' has died at the age of 36. Authorities are investigating her death, which reportedly showed no signs of foul play or trauma. The cause of death has not been disclosed, and tributes have poured in from fans and colleagues alike.

explore_lenses.label: What is confirmed about her death?
explore_lenses.title: Found unresponsive; no cause announced
explore_lenses.summary: Authorities said Panettiere was found unresponsive at a Greenville, South Carolina apartment on Sunday, August 16, and was pronounced dead after lifesaving efforts. Officials have said there were no preliminary indications of foul play or trauma, but have not identified a cause of death.

claims.text: Police said Panettiere was found unresponsive shortly before 2 p.m. Sunday and was pronounced dead at the scene after lifesaving measures.
The Greenville Police Department said its preliminary investigation found no signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances.
An autopsy found no signs of trauma, while no cause of death had been determined as of August 18.

explore_lenses.summary: The absence of apparent foul play or trauma is not a final explanation for the death. Investigators and the family’s representatives have said the case remains open, and officials have not authenticated circulating emergency-audio claims.

explore_lenses.label: Why does her death resonate so widely?
explore_lenses.title: A career spanning childhood TV to country music
explore_lenses.summary: Panettiere's audience crossed generations and genres: she began acting as a child, became closely identified with NBC's "Heroes," and later combined acting and singing in "Nashville." Her recent memoir also put her personal account of early fame, addiction and depression into public view without establishing any link to her death.

claims.text: Panettiere's role as Claire Bennet in "Heroes" propelled her to fame; she later earned two Golden Globe supporting-actress nominations for "Nashville."
She returned to film in "Scream VI" in 2023 after stepping away from acting for several years.
Her memoir, "This Is Me: A Reckoning," was published on May 19, 2026 and was described by its publisher as her account of her own life and career.
Connie Britton, Viola Davis, Melissa Barrera, Bethany Joy Lenz and Jay Shetty were among the public figures paying tribute, according to AP.

story_report.summary: Actor Hayden Panettiere, known for “Heroes” and “Nashville,” has died at 36. Police said she was found unresponsive shortly before 2 p.m. Sunday and pronounced dead at the scene after lifesaving measures. Authorities are investigating, though the Greenville Police Department said its preliminary findings showed no foul play or suspicious circumstances. An autopsy found no signs of trauma, and public figures including former colleagues have shared tributes.

sections.heading: Panettiere’s Screen Career
sections.body: Panettiere rose to prominence as Claire Bennet in “Heroes” and later received two Golden Globe supporting-actress nominations for “Nashville.” After several years away from acting, she returned to film in 2023’s “Scream VI.” Her memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” was published May 19, 2026 and was described by its publisher as an account of her life and career.

sections.heading: Panettiere Death Investigation Continues
sections.body: The death remained under investigation, and no cause of death had been determined as of Aug. 18. Panettiere’s publicist also said there was an ongoing investigation. Greenville Police told TIME that purported dispatch audio circulating online was not the department’s audio and could not be verified.

unresolved.text: The medical cause and manner of Panettiere’s death have not been publicly disclosed, and it is not known whether or when investigators or the coroner will release further findings.

Prosecutors allege that a former street gang leader, known as 'Keffe D,' orchestrated the attack as an act of revenge for the beating of his nephew. The trial marks a significant development in a case that has long been considered one of the most prominent cold cases in the U.S.
